statuses.positive_reply_definition: Any reply that says yes, asks for a time, asks a question about the work or the price, or books a call. 'Not now' with a date is neutral. 'Stop' or 'not interested' is negative.
statuses.only_kpi: A booked 15-minute call (or an agreed 20-minute visit for the local track). Replies are a leading sign, not the goal.

definitions.rates: reply_rate = replies/delivered; positive_rate = positive_replies/delivered; booked_rate = calls_booked/delivered; shown per variant, per phase, per track, and pooled per element (e.g. all batches that used subject 'Quick chat?')

design.when: On each phase's judge_on date (11 working days after the send day) and every Sunday at a 15-minute review. Also an early read on early_read_on (3 working days after send) used only to pick the provisional default for the next batch.
design.who: TENET drafts the entry from the app's data; Dayyan (and Jack for L and T) confirm the decision with one tap.

decision (carry A | carry B | no signal | rewrite | pause track)
provisional (true if made at the early read)
rules: A decision made at the early read is provisional and is confirmed or reversed on judge_on; a reversal applies to the batch after next, never retroactively.

Qualitative notes matter as much as counts at these volumes: what people actually wrote back decides wording more than 1 vs 0.

final_layout.rule: Per segment, pick each element (subject, opener, offer line, ask, sender voice, length, follow-up cadence, send day and time) from pooled counts across every batch that used it: most positive replies per delivered email wins; ties go to the simpler option. If a segment has fewer than 3 positive replies in total, the layout is recorded as 'best guess' with the reasons, not as a result.

dashboard_notes: Home (/phase1): today's batch only: a list of the emails leaving next (prospect, variant letter, subject, time), one Send/Queue button, and a 4-number scoreboard (sent, replies, positive, calls booked). Everything else behind tabs.
Queueing: 'Send' at the Wed/Thu evening meeting means 'approve the batch; it leaves at 08:45-09:45 tomorrow'. Show the next send time on the button.

Per prospect before send: company_type must be ltd/llp (or consent_recorded) and the email must match its source; otherwise the row is greyed with the reason. A 'stop' reply blocks the address and its domain everywhere.
Replies tab: inbound email matched by thread; a suggested playbook category and the drafted reply shown; nothing sent without a tap.
Metrics tab: counts by variant and phase, and pooled_by_element; a 'no signal' label whenever the two arms differ by fewer than 2 positive replies.
Review tab: the review_log entries; TENET fills a draft on judge_on and on Sundays; one tap confirms the decision.
Track T: no Send button; a visit list with 'visited / card left / consent recorded' toggles and a consent note (who, when, how).
Jack's sends: until his Gmail is connected, the Emails tab shows a copy button per message and a 'mark sent' toggle.
